text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm experimenting with an evict->flowback pattern to make eviction signals flow back into admission instead of being dropped. Idea: eviction becomes an explicit event admission can consume and degrade (or reshuffle) proactively. Wanted early feedback before I write an RFC.

rahul: Hmm interesting. High-level: why flowback vs just stronger eviction? worried about oscillations and fairness.

maya: Main drivers: 1) stop pointless evict->reload cycles that thrash KV cache, 2) allow admission to preemptively reshape windows (reduce microbatch size / divert to fallback model) based on eviction pressure, 3) map evictions to SLA-aware decisions instead of blind LRU.

lucas: KV warmup cost is my top concern. If eviction turns into admission churn we'll just move the cache pain earlier. How do you avoid shifting the tail?

maya: Good call. Plan: hysteresis + dampening + short tokenized warm grace for recently-warmed entries. Flowback carries metadata: tenant, evict_reason, last_warm_ts, deadline_hint. Admission uses deadline_hint + slab membership to decide. Quick pseudo:

```
// on eviction: emit(flowback{tenant, reason, warm_ts, hint})
admit(flowback f) {
  slab = slab_for(f.tenant)
  if slab.is_premium && now - f.warm_ts < WARM_GRACE: drop_evict()
  else if f.hint < SLAB_THRESHOLD: trigger_small_batch_fallback()
  else enqueue_normal()
}
```

anya: SLA mapping: how do you ensure enterprise routes don't see unpredictable latency if admission starts diverting them? we need deterministic contract for premium slabs.

maya: We keep strict slab contracts: premium slabs get strong headroom guarantees and never get redirection unless explicit degrade policy invoked (canary only). mid slabs get probabilistic redirection + explicit notify. Also we expose per-route admission knobs in console (headroom tokens, preemptive-divert=false/true).

rahul: Metrics we should track during proto: evict->flowback rate, rewarm rate, KV miss delta, 90/95/99 latency per slab, fairness index (Jain), oscillation count (tenant toggles per minute).

lucas: Rollout idea: start internal-only, 1% machines, synthetic hot tenants, measure rewarm cost. Add a quick kill switch to drop flowback path if we see thrash.

ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary for branch "evict-flowback/proto" to cluster staging at 2024-04-12T15:00Z :rocket:

maya: Test plan notes: microbench: 1) hot-tenant continuous stream vs baseline; 2) mixed traffic with short bursts; 3) prioritized premium route under pressure. Targets: rewarm overhead <10% and 95th latency no more than 5% worse for premium slab. Volunteers to help run experiments?

anya: I can own SLA contract surface and console flags. Will prepare knob list and UI copy.

rahul: I'll do the metrics + alerting dashboard. Will add an oscillation alert and KV miss alarm.

lucas: I'll build the synthetic workload harness and run the warm/cold migration tests.

maya: Awesome — thanks. I'll put a short RFC draft in the design docs folder and link here when ready. Prefer to land a minimal proto that only emits flowback events and a no-op admission consumer first (observe-only), then iterate.

maya: TL;DR: evict->flowback lets admission make smarter SLA-aware choices, but we need hysteresis, warm grace and careful rollout to avoid cache thrash. :white_check_mark:
